answerer_C.final_text: {"answer": "Ban Ki-moon was the Secretary-General of the United Nations in 2015. The South Korean diplomat served as the eighth UN Secretary-General from 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2016, spanning two five-year terms. 2015 was a landmark year of his tenure: the General Assembly adopted the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development (the Sustainable Development Goals) in September, and the Paris Agreement on climate change was concluded at COP21 in December. That same September, the General Assembly also adopted a resolution creating a more transparent framework for selecting the next Secretary-General. Ban was succeeded on 1 January 2017 by António Guterres of Portugal, the ninth Secretary-General."}
